name: SGLang RCE
tile_line: Exploited, no fix yet. Risky if the port is reachable.
tldr: SGLang, a popular AI model server, has bugs that let anyone who reaches its port run code or steal API keys, mostly with no login. NEAR AI says an unnamed SGLang bug was used to break into a server. No fixed release yet: keep it off untrusted networks.
summary: NEAR AI reported it on 9 Nov 2026 and has patched its own inference servers; SGLang itself hasn't released a fix.

affected.label: You run SGLang (any version)
affected.text: The CVE record for CVE-2026-15969 lists v0.5.15 and earlier, but no fixed version has been named. As of 24 Nov 2026 the advisories still list no patched version, and v0.5.23 (2 Nov) is the newest release. With no fixed release, treat every version as affected as a precaution.

affected.label: Its HTTP port is reachable by attackers
affected.text: By default SGLang listens only on 127.0.0.1, port 30000. You're exposed if it was started with --host 0.0.0.0, published from a container or Kubernetes, or put behind a proxy that forwards every route. API keys alone don't close it: the LoRA tensor route has no auth check when LoRA is on, and /server_info can leak the keys. Admin routes are open when no keys are set. Changes merged on 7 and 14 Nov stop /server_info leaking keys and make admin routes need an admin key (the current docs already describe this), but no release includes them yet.

do.label: Keep SGLang off untrusted networks
do.text: Bind it to 127.0.0.1 or a private network, segment inference hosts, and firewall the port. If clients must reach it, put a reverse proxy in front that allows only the inference routes you use and blocks everything else, including /server_info.

do.label: Set separate user and admin API keys
do.text: Start with both --api-key and --admin-api-key, and block /server_info, which gives the admin key to anyone holding the user key. This doesn't fix the LoRA tensor bug, so it's no substitute for network limits.

do.label: Turn off pickle IPC and unused features
do.text: Set SGLANG_USE_PICKLE_IPC to false (it defaults to true). Don't enable LoRA, the dumper (DUMPER_SERVER_PORT), remote weight updates or distributed weight routes unless you need them. Prefer safetensors and refuse untrusted .bin/.pt checkpoints.

do.label: Was it exposed? Rotate keys, check logs
do.text: /server_info returns the API keys and SSL key password, so rotate them. Make sure API keys and prompts aren't written to logs; NEAR AI lost two customers' API keys that way. Watch for an upstream fix and update when one ships.
